extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting papers to OSDI '26 (systems research conference)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and instructions for preparing and delivering manuscript PDFs for OSDI '26, including formatting, anonymization, file types, ethics, and page limits. Targets authors of systems research papers submitting to the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic PDF submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of all papers must be made electronically in PDF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send files meant for word-processing packages (Word, WordPerfect, LaTeX, Framemaker, etc.). If you are using Microsoft Word or LaTeX, use the templates on the conference paper templates page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper length / page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: No longer than 12 single-spaced 8.5" x 11" pages, including figures and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted papers that exceed these limits will be rejected without review. No deadline extensions will be granted for reformatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: References allowance (separate from page limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may include as many additional pages as needed for references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional pages for references are allowed, but additional pages are not permitted for supplementary material in appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: No supplementary material in appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted papers may not use extra pages for supplementary material in appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References may use extra pages, but appendices containing supplementary results or material are not allowed as extra pages; violating this will cause the submission to be out of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size and printable layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should make sure that their submission prints properly on US-style 8.5 x 11-inch paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All text and figures must fit inside a 7" x 9" (178 mm x 229 mm) block centered on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Columns and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use two columns separated by 0.33" (8 mm) of whitespace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the two-column layout and the specified whitespace are followed so text and figures remain within the required block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font size and type
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 10-point type on 12-point (single-spaced) leading and Times Roman or a similar font for the body of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to body text; other elements (captions, footnotes) should remain readable but conform to overall legibility and page-fit constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures, tables, and graphs legibility
rubrics_metrics.description: All graphs and figures should be readable when printed in black and white; figures and tables should be legible in black and white without requiring magnification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid color-only contrast cues; choose markers/line styles and sufficient resolution so printed B&W versions remain clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page numbering
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include page numbers so reviewers can reference specific pages; this is part of the required formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization and double-blind review
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper review process is double-blind. Authors must make a good-faith effort to anonymize their submissions and should not identify themselves either explicitly or by implication (e.g., through the references or acknowledgments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncertain about how to anonymize a submission, contact the program co-chairs well in advance. Submissions violating anonymization rules will not be considered for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting & anonymization enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions violating the detailed formatting and anonymization rules will not be considered for review; papers not meeting these criteria will be rejected without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program committee checks submissions against these requirements. Authors will not receive deadline extensions for reformatting or anonymization fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of templates and prohibited source files
rubrics_metrics.description: If using Microsoft Word or LaTeX, authors should use the conference paper templates. Do not send word-processing source files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide only the final PDF; follow template defaults to satisfy font, spacing, margins, and column requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct and out-of-band contact prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be no out-of-band contact between authors and program committee members. Authors must abide by the ACM Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserving review integrity is essential; violations of the ethics code may result in additional action by USENIX upon recommendation of the program co-chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing quality (recommended reading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to read resources on how to write a good paper and on sentence/paragraph clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested readings include 'An Evaluation of the Ninth SOSP Submissions; or, How (and How Not) to Write a Good Systems Paper' (Levin & Redell), 'The Science of Scientific Writing' (Gopen & Swan), and 'The Elements of Style' (Strunk & White). These are recommendations to improve clarity and quality, not formal requirements.
